Specification: This module constructs and optionally writes out a TLA+ action-trace module representing the current TLC counterexample trace. It is a utility-oriented specification that uses TLC-provided data such as CounterExample.action, folds over the recorded actions to synthesize EXTENDS declarations and a disjunctive _next operator, and then serializes the generated text to a file. The design is centered on trace extraction and pretty-printing rather than state-transition modeling: it defines helper operators for string assembly, checks whether a counterexample exists and whether console output is enabled, and if so writes a textual module whose action constraint follows the TLC level.
IfThenElse: IF "parameters" \in DOMAIN r THEN r.name \o "(" \o Params(r) \o ")" ELSE r.name

IF CounterExample.action = {} \/ ("console" \in DOMAIN CounterExample /\ CounterExample["console"] = FALSE) THEN TRUE ELSE /\ Serialize(_TLCTraceModule, _TLCTraceFile, [format |-> "TXT", charset |-> "UTF-8", openOptions |-> <<"WRITE", "CREATE", "TRUNCATE_EXISTING">>]).exitValue = 0 /\ PrintT("CounterExample written: " \o _TLCTraceFile)
FunctionApplication: FoldSet(LAMBDA module, acc: acc \o (IF acc = "" THEN "EXTENDS " ELSE ", ") \o module, "", M)
FoldLeft(LAMBDA acc, p: acc \o (IF acc = "" THEN "" ELSE ", ") \o ToString(r.context[p]), "", r.parameters)

DivisionNotes: _TLCTrace is classified as a StatePredicate: it is Boolean-valued, contains no primed variables, and contains no temporal operators. Although it performs TLC-side effects through Serialize and PrintT, syntactically it is not an action operator because there are no primed variables or temporal constructs.
_extends, _next, and _TLCTraceModule are placed in ValueDef because they compute strings or other non-Boolean helper values rather than actions or temporal formulas.
